# Thanksgiving Hymns Column 27 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** 1QHa (Cave 1), Col. 27 | **Condition:** very fragmentary

---

**1** [...] everything [...] You made for Your glory, and [...] according to [...]

**2** [...] the vast array of Your works, and You assigned [...] to serve [...]

**3** [...] Your truth. And You set the course of generations [...] through all [...]

**4** [...] the ages of eternity, and the rhythms of [...] You planned [...]

**5** [...] to walk in Your presence in the land of the living, and You opened [...]

**6** [...] the springs of [...] for Your servant, and the source of [...] truth [...]

**7** [...] all for the sake of Your glory. And You breathed into being [...]

**8** [...] every living creature, and You determined how each one would act [...]

**9** [...] and the powerful ones who fulfill Your will, and [...] for Your glory [...]

**10** [...] You brought into being [...] for Your honor and for the glory of Your name [...]

**11** [...] and the spirits [...] You gave each one its appointed task [...]

**12** [...] among the holy ones, and [...] the armies of angels [...]

**13** [...] You assigned their duties before Your glorious presence [...]

**14** [...] and the rulers of [...] within their realms [...]

**15** [...] the great lights according to their hidden patterns, and the stars [...]

**16** [...] the winds according to the laws set for them, and everything they do [...]

**17** [...] generation after generation, and the vaults of [...]

**18** [...] lightning and snow and [...] ice [...]

**19** [...] each arriving in its season for [...] Your purpose [...]

**20** [...] because You made all of it for Your glory [...]

---

*PNEUMA notes: Column 27 is very fragmentary, near the end of the scroll. Even in its broken state, the theological vision shines through: everything from angels to ice exists for the Creator's glory. The cosmic scope — spirits, stars, winds, weather — echoes the creation theology of Column 21, bringing the scroll full circle. Dynamic rendering preserves the hymnic sweep of the original.*
